analysis:
All three units are CHANGELOG.md text: two base excerpts (lines 1327-1791) and the head excerpt (lines 1-227). No code is visible, so nothing is verified against source. Security-relevant claims in the head text:
- Lines 24-33: demanded prefix-cache reuse. This includes SSD write share for repeated checkpoints and short-prefix boundary capture for dense Qwen, Nemotron and Bonsai. It may interact with T-041's per-donation gate (adoption bound + 1,024-token floor, 30-minute TTL). The next pass should check SSDPrefixCache.donate and SSDPrefixCachePolicy for any relaxation.
- Lines 39-49: Autopilot daily earnings floor, matching the T-060 reward-administration boundary. It adds admin funding and baseline-repair endpoints, an independent pool cap, an end date of 2026-11-07, and a consent journal (lines 19-22) that no longer takes the inventory write lock.
- Lines 88-89 and 123-128: SSD write-budget ledger, migration timeouts, and soft-delete mutations gated by a default-off flag.
- Lines 134-152: account erasure, relevant to T-059.
- Lines 17 and 72-81: AI-assisted merge clearance for Layr-Labs members. This is CI/process and arguably outside the threat-model scope.
- Lines 91-95: typical MTP acceptance is now the default, so sampled output is approximate. This is not a security regression per se.
No concrete regression is confirmed from the changelog alone.

findings.detail: The head CHANGELOG says repeated authenticated checkpoints get access to a reserved SSD write share on first local appearance (line 27). It also says one aligned demanded boundary is captured below the normal solo stripe so that 'repeated short prefixes can be published for reuse' (line 29). T-041 and its detection_hint state that a donation persists only when the whole-block prefix exceeds the model's adoption bound plus a 1,024-token benefit floor. They also say that loosening this gate widens the at-rest surface and needs a fresh SEC-035 sign-off. Only the changelog is visible here, so I cannot confirm whether the code relaxes the gate. If shorter prefixes are written to the encrypted SSD tier, more short and potentially repeated prefixes persist for the 30-minute TTL. That widens the same-account TTFT oracle and at-rest metadata exposure (file counts, mtimes) without the recorded review. Fix: confirm whether the SSDPrefixCache.donate gate changed. If it did, update T-041 and record a SEC-035 sign-off. If it did not, clarify the changelog wording so it does not imply short-prefix SSD persistence.
findings.title: Changelog describes broader SSD prefix-cache donations than T-041's per-donation gate records
